macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rally after weak jobs report
items.summary: The Nasdaq rose 1.2% to 27,190, the S&P 500 gained 0.7% to 7,722, and the Dow advanced 0.5% to 51,176 after September payroll growth came in well below expectations.[1]

items.title: Weak employment data reduces Fed hike expectations
items.summary: The U.S. added 29,000 jobs in September and unemployment rose to 4.2%, easing expectations for an October Federal Reserve rate increase. Fed funds futures indicated a 22.7% probability of a 25-basis-point hike, down from 64.2% a week earlier.[1]

items.title: Nvidia reaches another record high
items.summary: Nvidia shares hit a new all-time high as investors continued to respond to the company’s expanded $150 billion stock-buyback authorization.[1]

items.title: Tesla deliveries beat expectations
items.summary: Tesla shares gained 4.5% after the automaker reported third-quarter deliveries above Wall Street forecasts, while Rivian fell 3.1% after its delivery performance failed to satisfy analysts.[1]

items.title: Nike underperforms after quarterly results
items.summary: Nike was the weakest Dow component after reporting fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue slightly below analysts’ expectations, although earnings matched consensus.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly reaches $87,000 as crypto market gains
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly climbed to about $87,000 as weak U.S. jobs data pushed bond yields lower. Ether and Solana also rose, while market activity remained mixed across major tokens.[2][4]

items.title: SEC proposes crypto custody framework for advisers and funds
items.summary: The SEC proposed rules governing how investment advisers and regulated funds may custody crypto assets, including conditions under which advisers and state trust companies could provide custody. The proposal would open a 60-day public-comment period after Federal Register publication.[4][7]

items.title: Community banks sue OCC over crypto trust charters
items.summary: The Independent Community Bankers of America sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, arguing that the agency lacks authority to grant national trust charters to crypto firms and has created unequal regulatory obligations.[4][5]

items.title: Blast plans to wind down Ethereum layer-2 network
items.summary: Blast said it plans to wind down its Ethereum layer-2 network after operating costs exceeded revenue, making the shutdown the most-covered project-development story in the latest crypto news cycle.[2]

items.title: NEAR Intents reports $3.8 million exploit
items.summary: NEAR Intents reported a roughly $3.8 million exploit, said it had identified the attacker, and issued a 48-hour ultimatum. A separate third-party adapter exploit drained about $305,000 from an Aave-related system, while Aave said its V3 protocol was unaffected.[3]

items.title: Bitget hack linked to North Korea in reported $387 million loss
items.summary: Coverage linked the reported $387 million Bitget hack to North Korea, with investigations also highlighting the use of artificial intelligence to trace the stolen funds.[1][3]

items.title: Fiserv launches Solana settlement coin for North Dakota bank
items.summary: Fiserv took Roughrider Coin live on Solana for bank settlement in North Dakota, marking a notable institutional blockchain deployment.[4][5]

items.title: SEC-approved leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETPs await trading
items.summary: The SEC approved 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ether exchange-traded products, though trading had not yet begun at the time of reporting.[2]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony Pictures reportedly wins Battlefield film rights
items.summary: Sony Pictures reportedly won a bidding war for a film adaptation of Battlefield, with Christopher McQuarrie attached to direct and Michael B. Jordan set to star. Production has not begun and no release date has been announced.

items.title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance expansion revealed
items.summary: Capcom showed new footage of the Ascendance expansion at Tokyo Game Show 2026, highlighting floating archipelagos, the new Araketa monster, returning Teostra, and the Boost Bracer mechanic.

items.title: Aion 2 tops Steam sales during advanced access
items.summary: Aion 2 reached Steam’s Global Top Sellers chart during advanced access and reportedly peaked at 171,530 concurrent players on September 30, while ranking first in eight countries.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day makes early Steam impact
items.summary: The Gears of War prequel launched with strong early performance and reportedly set a Steam record, returning to Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago’s early years during the Locust War.

items.title: AOC announces 1,050Hz esports monitor
items.summary: AOC announced the AGON PRO AGP257FT, a Full HD gaming monitor capable of an overclocked 1,050Hz refresh rate aimed at competitive esports players.

items.title: Ubisoft unveils March of the Giants MOBA
items.summary: Ubisoft reportedly revealed March of the Giants, a MOBA built around commanding armies rather than controlling individual heroes.

items.title: Gaming industry seeks clearer Indian regulation
items.summary: India’s gaming industry is asking the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to distinguish video games from real-money games in regulation.
